definition: The legendary founder of Gojoseon, born to the bear woman Ungnyeo and the heavenly prince Hwanung. Tradition dates his reign to 2333 BCE, and he is later remembered as a mountain god.
The first Korean kingdom in traditional history, said to have been founded by Dangun in 2333 BCE. Its historicity and borders are debated, and it is also called Old Joseon.
A thirteenth-century collection compiled by the Buddhist monk Iryeon, preserving foundation myths, legends and Buddhist traditions. It is the earliest surviving full account of the Dangun story.
The bear woman of the Dangun myth. She endured a test of mugwort, garlic and darkness, became human, and bore Dangun, the founder of Gojoseon.
The foods Hwanung gave the bear and tiger in the Dangun story. Eating only these and avoiding sunlight for one hundred days was the test of transformation.
A Korean shamanic ritual in which a mudang invites gods and spirits, often through song, dance and offerings. Gut may heal, celebrate, or guide the dead, and it is still performed today.
The abandoned seventh daughter of a king in Korean shamanic narrative. She journeys to the land of the dead, obtains the water of life, and becomes the first shaman and guide of souls.
The ruler of the sea in Korean folktales, living in an underwater palace. He can be generous or foolish, and he appears in the rabbit tale and in Sim Cheong.
A celestial woman who descends to earth in Korean folktale, often to bathe in a mountain pool. In the woodcutter tale, one is stranded when her robe is hidden.
A Korean narrative performance in which a singer and a drummer tell a long story through song and speech. Simcheongga is one of the five surviving pansori repertory pieces.
